title: Policy boundary evidence playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines how Redwood builds, packages, and presents compliance evidence for "policy boundaries" — the discrete authorization, residency, and audit controls that separate regulated workloads from general-purpose inference traffic. It unifies RBAC/audit/data-residency artifacts, incident-response evidence capture, and secure-SDLC touchpoints into a repeatable handoff process for audits and exception reviews.

Audience and intent:
- Primary: Security, Compliance, Legal, and Engineering teams responsible for preparing and defending regulatory evidence for deployments (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Secondary: Customer-facing teams (sales, CSM) who need artifact packages for enterprise reviews.

Scope:
- Applies to: model-serving routes, dedicated GPU pools, and private deployment control planes that host regulated customer data or have residency constraints.
- Excludes: ephemeral developer sandboxes with no customer data (see Appendix A for criteria).

Key principles:
- Evidence-first: every deployment that claims isolation or residency must have a minimal evidence bundle assembled before acceptance testing.
- Immutable provenance: artifacts must include event timestamps, signer identity, and immutable identifiers (deployment-id, artifact-hash).
- Separation of concerns: RBAC decisions, audit logs, and data residency manifests are gathered independently and stitched into a single evidence packet.

Roles & ownership:
- Security (owner): craft evidence templates, validate artifacts, run pre-audit checks.
- Eng-Platform (producer): generate runtime attestations (service-identity, network policy, routing table).
- Eng-Infra (producer): provide KMS/HSM remit and key rotation logs, host-level audit stream.
- Compliance (consumer): review packet and raise exceptions/acceptance.
- Customer Success (distributor): deliver accepted artifacts to customers under NDA.

Minimum evidence bundle (required items):
1) Access matrix snapshot (RBAC)
- CSV: role, principal, scope, granted_at, grant_source, request_ticket
- Signed by: eng-platform-service-account (detached signature)

2) Authorization decision log slice (audit)
- Time-bounded event slice (start / end) in JSON Lines format; include request_id, actor, resource, decision, policy_version, reason_code
- Retention note: slice must be preserved for a minimum of 90 days for onboarding review, 365 days for regulated customers.

3) Deployment residency manifest (data residency & retention)
- YAML/JSON showing region codes, storage class, retention policy id, legal-hold flag, and data-flow diagram reference (artifact-id).

4) Secure-SDLC attestations
- Commit range and CI pipeline run IDs used to build the service image, SBOM, and test-suite summary with pass/fail for regression prompts and privacy tests.

5) Incident-response snapshot (if applicable)
- If an incident has occurred in the preceding 30 days: incident-id, timeline, preserved forensic logs, and chain-of-custody notes.

6) Evidence manifest (index)
- Single file listing artifact filenames, sha256 hashes, creators, and signed timestamps.

Pre-assembly checks (automated):
- RBAC completeness: verify no active principal has wildcard scope against residency-controlled routes. Failure threshold: any wildcard => fail.
- Audit completeness: query audit-stream for gapless sequence numbers for the slice time range; missing events > 1% => fail.
- Residency policy match: declared regions must have active network egress rules blocking external regions; test with e2e traffic-sim.
- SBOM presence: image SBOM must be present and not reference disallowed packages (see blacklist).

Playbook: building an evidence packet (step-by-step)
1) Request creation (owner: Eng-Platform)
- Create packet request in EvidenceTracker with fields: deployment-id, customer, policy-boundary-id, intended-audit-window.

2) Artifact collection (owner: Eng-Platform + Eng-Infra)
- Export RBAC snapshot: run `infra-tools rbac:export --deployment-id $DEPLOYMENT_ID --since $START --until $END --format csv`
- Export authz events: `audit-query --deployment $DEPLOYMENT_ID --from $START --to $END --out events.jsonl`
- Export residency manifest: `residency-manifest --deployment $DEPLOYMENT_ID > residency.json`
- Export secure-sdlc attestations: link CI run IDs and provide SBOM zip.

3) Integrity and signing (owner: Security)
- Generate manifest: `evidence-manifest --add *.json *.csv *.jsonl --out manifest.json`
- Calculate hashes: sha256 for each artifact and add to manifest.
- Sign manifest: `signtool sign --key /kms/evidence-signing-key --in manifest.json --out manifest.sig`

4) Validation (owner: Security)
- Run automated pre-assembly checks.
- Run human review for any flagged items (see triage thresholds below).

5) Packaging and delivery (owner: Compliance/CSM)
- Produce encrypted bundle: `tar czf bundle.tar.gz --files-from manifest.json && kms-encrypt --key customer-kek bundle.tar.gz > bundle.enc`
- Deliver: upload to secure artifact repo and share link to authorized reviewers.

Triage thresholds and escalation:
- High-risk flags (require immediate stop and remediation):
  - RBAC wildcard found for residency-protected route.
  - Missing audit sequence numbers > 1% for the selected window.
  - KMS key rotation failure in last 7 days tied to the deployment.
- Medium-risk (require remediation within 7 days):
  - SBOM contains package with high CVE and no approved mitigations.
  - Evidence missing CI pipeline run ID for the exact image tagged in production.
- Low-risk (document and schedule remediation):
  - Minor telemetry gaps non-overlapping with target window.

Incident-response integration:
- When an incident is opened against a policy boundary, attach the current evidence packet, then:
  1) Freeze outgoing deliveries for the affected boundary.
  2) Snapshot live audit streams to WORM storage.
  3) Assign forensics owner and log chain-of-custody.
  4) If customer data may have been exposed, follow the legal notification workflow (see incident-notification-template in related pages).

Audit and retention mapping:
- Short-term: packet snapshots stored for 2 years in secure evidence repo (default).
- Long-term (regulated customers): 7–10 years depending on jurisdiction (see residency-manifest policy-id mapping).
- Access to stored packets: RBAC-protected; reviewers must request temporary access via EvidenceTracker and acceptance is logged.

Examples and templates:
- Authorization event example (JSONL single line):
  {"ts":"2026-01-10T15:23:12Z","request_id":"r-84b3c...","actor":"service-account:eng-platform","resource":"deployment:dp-1234:route:/inference/secure","decision":"DENY","policy_version":"v2025-11-03","reason":"residency_violation"}

- Minimal manifest example (manifest.json):
  {"artifacts": [
      {"name": "rbac.csv", "sha256": "<sha256>"},
      {"name": "events.jsonl", "sha256": "<sha256>"},
      {"name": "residency.json", "sha256": "<sha256>"}
    ],
    "signed_by": "security@redwood",
    "signed_at": "2026-02-10T12:00:00Z"
  }

Appendix A — Exemption criteria (when a boundary does not need a full packet):
- Internal dev sandbox limited to 24-hour lifetime and no PII or customer data used.
- Test-only model endpoints explicitly flagged and isolated with NX routing and blocked from external ingress.

Appendix B — Frequently used commands and utilities:
- infra-tools rbac:export (CSV export)
- audit-query (time-bound JSONL extraction)
- residency-manifest (exports region/retention mapping)
- evidence-manifest and signtool (integrity and signing)

Related artifacts and references:
- EvidenceTracker playbook (link internal)
- Audit schema contract (../audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025.json)
- Authorization logging patterns (../rbac-and-auth/authorization-logging-and-deprovisioning-guidance-2026.json)

Change history and governance:
- Template and rules reviewed by Security and Compliance quarterly. Significant changes require sign-off from Head of Security and Director, Compliance.

Contact and escalation:
- On-call security lead: pager redwood-sec-oncall (contact details in team roster).
- Evidence exceptions: exceptions@redwood-inference.com (tickets routed to Governance board).

Document owners: Security (primary), Eng-Platform (secondary).
